chunk_findings.detail: `doctor_notes(repo)` is documented — and used elsewhere for `identity_notes(repo)`, `bare_notes(repo)`, `stale_primary_notes(repo)` — as producing notes *for the repository at `repo`*, but the new call ignores the parameter and passes the raw process working directory: `TB.stale_notes(Path.cwd())`. The intent states the warning is about "the active ddflow package path is outside the **current worktree**", i.e. the worktree that contains the invocation, not the literal cwd. Concrete failure: run `ddflow doctor` from a subdirectory of the primary repo (e.g. `/repo/src`). The discovered repo root passed in as `repo` is `/repo`, but `Path.cwd()` is `/repo/src`, so the package-path containment check is evaluated against `/repo/src`; the primary's own venv package is then "outside" that path and doctor emits a spurious "the ddflow running is not the tree's own" note for a perfectly correct primary-tree invocation. The symmetric case — a caller invoking `doctor_notes(<other repo>)` from an unrelated cwd — silently reports the note for the wrong tree (false negative when the branch worktree is the one being inspected). The check needs the worktree/repo root (the `repo` argument, or a git-derived root), not `Path.cwd()`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/repo_hygiene.py:128 (`doctor_notes`)

chunk_findings.detail: The shim promises (docstring line 8: "running it ... makes the branch's code the one that runs") but it only sets `PYTHONPATH` and never changes directory. With `python -m ddflow`, CPython inserts the *current directory* at the front of `sys.path` (same rule as `-c`), ahead of `PYTHONPATH`. So the tree's package only wins if the shim happens to be invoked from a directory that does not itself contain a `ddflow/` package. Concretely: the user is in the primary checkout (where they ran `ddflow claim`) and runs the absolute shim path the claim just printed, `<wt>/.ddflow/local/bin/ddflow --json next`. `sys.path[0]` is the primary's cwd, `<primary>/ddflow/__init__.py` is imported, and `PYTHONPATH=<wt>` is never consulted — i.e. the exact bug this change exists to fix (manual check tests main's code) reproduces silently, and the user has no signal because the shim reports success. The same happens when running worktree A's shim while cwd is worktree B. A one-line `cd` (`exec` should at least `cd "$tree"` or use `python -P`/`-I`-style path control, or export `PYTHONPATH` while invoking the console entry point instead of `-m`) would be needed for the shim to be location-independent the way the advice text advertises.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/tree_bin.py:33 (write_shim body)

chunk_findings.detail: The final line, `assert sys.executable`, is a tautology: `sys.executable` is a non-empty string in every CPython runtime (and the test process would not exist without an interpreter), so this assertion can never fail and contributes no coverage to the test it terminates. If the intent was to verify that the shim/doctor code under test runs the *same* interpreter as the test process, that check is absent — e.g. a `write_shim`/`advice` implementation that hard-codes `/usr/bin/python3` (or a primary venv's python) instead of `sys.executable` would still pass this test, which is precisely the class of "runs the wrong tree/interpreter" bug the change is meant to prevent. Relatedly, line 44 feeds `PA.package_parent()` — the directory that contains the running package — into `stale_notes`, so it only ever exercises the trivially-contained case; it never passes an actual claimed-worktree root, so a `doctor` that fails to warn when invoked from a worktree would not be caught by this test.

chunk_findings.detail: The fix is applied as an *environment variable* on the exec'd interpreter, not as an interpreter flag. `PYTHONSAFEPATH` is read by every CPython start-up and, unlike `-P`, it is inherited by every process the shim (transitively) spawns. The old shim already leaked `PYTHONPATH`, but `PYTHONPATH` only *adds* the tree; `PYTHONSAFEPATH=1` *removes* the implicit `sys.path[0] = cwd` from all descendants, which is a semantic change to processes that have nothing to do with running ddflow. Concretely: a user runs the shimmed `ddflow` from inside the worktree, and `ddflow gate` (or a hook, or `ddflow acp --wrap`) launches the project's test command `python -m pytest` with cwd = repo root. Before this change that child had the repo root on `sys.path` (the documented `-m`/`-c` rule), so tests doing `import mytool` for a root-level module resolved; after this change the child inherits `PYTHONSAFEPATH=1`, cwd is dropped, and those imports raise `ModuleNotFoundError` — the gate fails for a reason unrelated to the branch's code. Using `exec <python> -P -m ddflow "$@"` (or otherwise unsetting the variable for the child environment) would confine the safe-path behaviour to the shim's own interpreter while still solving the reported shadowing problem.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/tree_bin.py:35 (`write_shim` body / `PYTHONSAFEPATH=1`)

evidence.diff_source: delta review of 1 commit since c9ab7c99e8

chunk_findings.detail: `doctor_notes(repo)` is documented and depended upon as producing notes *for the repository at `repo`*, but the new entry is computed from `Path.cwd()` and ignores the `repo` argument entirely. Any caller that inspects a repository other than the process working directory — e.g. `ddflow doctor` invoked with an explicit repo/worktree path, a script that audits several worktrees in a loop, or a test calling `doctor_notes(tmp_path)` — now gets the stale-package verdict for whatever directory the process happens to stand in, not for the tree being examined. Concretely: run the command from the primary while passing a claimed worktree's path and the worktree is reported as "ddflow running is not the tree's own" even though the running package may be that worktree's; run it from an unrelated directory and the real mismatch in `repo` is silently missed. The check should be derived from `repo` (the tree being diagnosed), not from ambient `cwd`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/repo_hygiene.py:125 (repo_hygiene.doctor_notes)

chunk_findings.detail: The generated shim is `<python> -P -m ddflow "$@"`, but `-P` exists only in Python 3.11+ (it was added together with `PYTHONSAFEPATH`). `sys.executable` is whatever interpreter is running the claim, and `write_shim` never checks its version. On a Python 3.10 (or older) environment the shim it writes is `<python> -P -m ddflow "$@"`, and running it prints `Unknown option: -P` and exits 2 — the branch's code is never executed, and because the failure is in the child interpreter the claim/doctor advice gives no hint. The `from __future__ import annotations` at the top of this very file (needed only for the PEP 604 `Path | None` annotation on interpreters below 3.10) indicates the codebase still tolerates interpreters where `-P` is not accepted, so "the shim runs the tree's code" is not true on those. If the shim is meant to be robust for any interpreter that can run ddflow, the cwd shadowing `-P` guards against should be handled differently (e.g. `-c 'import sys; sys.path.insert(0,...)'` or dropping `-P` and clearing the cwd entry), or the requirement must be enforced and reported.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/tree_bin.py:36

chunk_findings.detail: `write_shim` swallows every `OSError` and returns `None`, and `advice` (line 46) then returns `""`, so `with_advice` silently emits no shim line: the claim succeeds, prints only its normal advice, and the operator does exactly what this change exists to prevent — runs the `ddflow` on PATH and tests the primary's code, with no indication that anything was skipped. The trigger is any write failure, e.g. `fsio.atomic_write` raising `FileNotFoundError`/`PermissionError` (`<tree>/.ddflow/local/bin` is a new directory this module never creates, and `.ddflow/local/` may be read-only or owned by another user). The same swallow also degrades the doctor path: `stale_notes` (line 60) falls back to the generic `'a claim-made shim'` because `shim.is_file()` is false, so the "use the shim" instruction points at a file that does not exist, instead of surfacing the failure that produced it.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/tree_bin.py:38-42

chunk_findings.detail: Context note first: the diff I can see is only a golden-transcript fixture update — the `agent_brief` entry's `chars` moves from `3210` to `3348`, a delta of 138 characters. That fixture is the *expected* output of a recorded run; on its own it asserts nothing about the code path it is supposed to guard. Nothing in the visible hunk pins the new value to a real behavioral change, so the risk is that the fixture was hand-edited to match whatever the implementation currently emits rather than the behavior described in the intent (claim printing/exporting a worktree-scoped run command, doctor warning when the active ddflow package path is outside the worktree). If the new 138 characters contain, e.g., an absolute path, a worktree path, or a host/PATH-dependent string, the fixture will silently drift on other machines, and because the surrounding list is byte-exact JSON with `<pkg>` placeholders only for paths under the package, any interpolation of the *current worktree* path would be non-deterministic. I cannot demonstrate the concrete input from this part of the diff alone (only 1 of 4 parts is visible), so I flag it as a risk rather than a confirmed defect.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_uc_surf_setup_ops_transcript.json (agent_brief entry)
